key_insight: Specialized, physics-driven machine learning force fields are needed to reliably model complex materials dynamics beyond the near-equilibrium regime where general-purpose MLIPs are strongest.
engineering_relevance: For practical atomistic simulation workflows, the main design challenge is balancing accuracy, nonlocal physics, and hardware cost while validating each model against the specific observable of interest.
method: Evaluate MLIP specialization for difficult dynamical regimes rather than only near-equilibrium benchmarks.
Compare architectural trade-offs in undersampled strained states, high-order message passing cost, and nonlocal interaction requirements.
Use observable-specific validation across electrified interfaces, open systems, multiphase evolution, and fracture.
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes evidence across four demanding application contexts and emphasizes benchmarking against intended observables rather than relying on zero-shot generalization alone.
watch_item: Task-specific potentials may improve target performance but can fail outside their training distribution, so extrapolation and computational scaling must be checked carefully.
paper_title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
